name.text: Forming an inequality for a line passing through the origin

questiontext.text:
A registered youth self-help group in Eldoret runs an environmental initiative upcycling shredded plastic waste into heavy-duty fencing posts. To ensure the posts are structurally durable, the weight of the binding compound mix (\(y\) kg) is strictly limited relative to the weight of the shredded plastic core (\(x\) kg).

Examine the structural safety graph below. Formulate the correct algebraic inequality represented by the shaded permissible manufacturing territory.

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

To form the inequality from the graph, we follow the systematic steps:

1. Identify the boundary line equation

The graph passes directly through the origin, so the \(y\)-intercept is \( 0 \). Because both intercepts are at \((0,0)\), we must use the second labeled point \( ({@x_pt@}, {@y_pt@}) \) to calculate the slope (\(m\)):

\( \displaystyle m = \frac{{@y_pt@} - 0}{{@x_pt@} - 0} = {@m@} \)

With a slope of \({@m@}\) and no constant term, the boundary line equation is \( y = {@m@}x \).

2. Determine the inequality symbol

The boundary line is drawn as a solid line, meaning the relationship is inclusive. We must use either \( \le \) or \( \ge \).

3. Identify the shaded region

The shaded area is situated below and to the right of the boundary line. This indicates that the permissible binding compound weight (\(y\)) must be less than or equal to the boundary. Therefore, we use the \( \le \) symbol:

\( \displaystyle \boxed{{@ta3@}} \)

4. Verify with a test point

Because the boundary line passes through the origin, we cannot use \((0,0)\) as a test point. Instead, we select a point clearly inside the shaded region, such as \( ({@x_pt@}, 0) \). Substituting \(x = {@x_pt@}\) and \(y = 0\):

\( \displaystyle \begin{aligned} y &\le {@m@}x \\ 0 &\le {@m@}({@x_pt@}) \\ 0 &\le {@y_pt@} \end{aligned} \)

This statement is true, confirming our algebraic inequality perfectly models the manufacturing constraints.
